purpose: Ground truth for tools/holdout_eval.py: which solved chains share a MECHANISM FAMILY, meaning the move that OPENS one would be a live hypothesis on the other.
why_not_the_filing: The metric previously read the card->class filing in skills/*/field-notes.md, widened by confusable_with. Two problems. First the filing is wrong for several cards, because classify_card scored the whole card at once and the exploit narrative outvoted the opener: a chain opening on a recursive merge into an object was filed under SSRF, one opening on bcrypt truncation under request smuggling. Second, and worse, a retrieval approach that keys on that same filing then scores well for agreeing with the labels the metric is defined over. The winning approach in the 2026-09-26 bake-off disclosed exactly that leak itself and said its leak-free number was 0.083, not the 0.208 it reported.
method: Three annotators labelled the 24 handout-backed cards independently and blind: they read only knowledge/chains/*.json and were forbidden from opening skills/*/field-notes.md or using bug-class names. 33 distinct pairs were proposed; a pair is recorded here only when at least two of the three agreed. Ten of the eleven were unanimous.
what_was_refused: cards that merely END the same way. Four chains finish holding a forged session token from four unrelated openings; pairing them would reward a retriever for matching endings.
cards sharing a late sub-mechanism. An unsanitised filename joined onto a directory appears in four chains but is the OPENING of only two.

percetron with novacore, although their preconditions read alike: percetron's card records path-shape bypasses as measured dead, so returning novacore there would propose the one thing that challenge already ruled out.
asymmetry_note: The race group is deliberately non-transitive: apexsurvive and ssos each pair with phantomfeed but not with each other, because phantomfeed genuinely carries both race shapes while the other two do not. Do not close this into a clique.

opening_mechanisms.htb-apexsurvive-profile-race-template-li: A state-changing sequence is not atomic: "race the profile update so an interleaved commit lands between the update and the token re-read" — "the token is fetched after the profile is committed, in a different function". The opening purchase is concurrency, not the XSS that follows.
opening_mechanisms.htb-artificial-university-grpc-attribute: Untrusted structure reaches an object merge: "look for a recursive merge whose destination is an object rather than a dict, and then grep the same class for eval/exec/system reading an attribute that merge could create" — attacker keys land in __dict__ of a long-lived service object and a sibling method feeds one of them to eval.
opening_mechanisms.htb-bobbys-bistro-sqli-jwks-write-chamel: A query filter is built by string formatting despite an ORM: "grep for text(), execute() and format/f-strings inside query construction" — filter(text("col='{}'".format(x))) is plain concatenation, so a tautology reads whatever columns the view renders.
opening_mechanisms.htb-bonechewercon-jku-forge-csp-injectio: A destination allowlist is enforced by string surgery instead of by the parser that will actually fetch: "compare the validator's host extraction with the HTTP client's: here domain=netloc.split('@')[1] vs requests' urlsplit().hostname=rpartition('@')[2]; abuse the disagreement with https://abc@localhost@ATTACKER/jwks.json" — the token names its own key source and the check that should confine it reads the URL differently.
opening_mechanisms.htb-bonechewercon-method-not-allowed-who: Make the application throw where it has no handler and read what the error path prints: "submit the form exactly as declared, even if the route looks unlikely to accept that method", then "enumerate the labelled detail sections of the error page" — the environment table is the configuration file verbatim.
opening_mechanisms.htb-encodecept-charset-xss-cache-decepti: The cache key does not capture what decides the response: "the cache key is the URI plus the extension, so an authenticated page can be stored under a static-looking URL" — confirmed by requesting /path.html?cb=N twice for MISS then HIT and reading it back anonymously, because the backend treats the dot as a format delimiter and ignores what the proxy keyed on.
opening_mechanisms.htb-imagetok-bcrypt-truncation-phar-soap: The signature does not cover all of the signed data: "bcrypt hashes only the first 72 bytes of its input, so with a 15-byte secret everything past json[57] is unauthenticated" — pad the leading field until the target field starts past the boundary, rewrite it and reuse the original signature verbatim.
opening_mechanisms.htb-neurosync-next-middleware-bypass-cur: One front layer is the whole authorization story and its decision is keyed on a header the client can supply: "send the framework's internal-subrequest header on a protected route and compare against the same route without it" — found by reading the pinned version against its published bypass advisory, after which no route re-checks auth.
opening_mechanisms.htb-nomad-notes-replace-pattern-nonce-re: The renderer's own substitution semantics are the bug: "if substitution is done with String.replace(pattern, value) then the $ replacement patterns are live - $-backtick expands to the text before the match", so checking the substitution order against key order lets a user field copy the nonce that was substituted earlier on the same line.
opening_mechanisms.htb-notebook-converter-pro-embed-images-: An attacker-supplied path inside an uploaded document reaches the filesystem unconfined: "upload a notebook whose markdown cell references a local path as an image and convert to html" — embed_images inlines the referenced file as base64 in the response; the same pipeline later writes wherever an unsanitised attachment key points.
opening_mechanisms.htb-novacore-hopbyhop-cache-overflow-dom: The app trusts a header the proxy is expected to set, and the client decides whether it survives: "list the proxy-added header in the Connection header so the proxy strips its own header before forwarding" — "the application treats a request with no proxy header as local and skips the token check".
opening_mechanisms.htb-omniwatch-varnish-urlless-cachekey-z: The cache key omits what the response depends on: "read the cache configuration before the application. Write down exactly what the hash function feeds in" — a hash that omits the URL and keys on a client-controlled header means one cacheable response answers every path, and a branch returning hash for a cookie-bearing path marks the page to share.
opening_mechanisms.htb-percetron-status-mirror-haproxy-tunn: The front proxy stops parsing and starts relaying raw bytes, so a second request never meets the gate: "point the status-mirroring route at an attacker server that answers a bare 101 Switching Protocols" then "write the second request onto the same socket immediately, addressed to the denied path" — path-shape bypasses were measured dead first.
opening_mechanisms.htb-phantomfeed-redos-verification-race-: A create-then-disable sequence is not atomic, and the slow step in between is attacker-controlled: "read the registration order and check whether the row is written before the flag that disables it", then widen the window with a validator whose cost is exponential in input length and fire the logins concurrently.
opening_mechanisms.htb-pod-diagnostics-arg-cache-key-duplic: The cache key is a subset of the request: "read the proxy's cache key before anything else and note every request attribute it leaves out", then "repeat that argument; the proxy keys on the first value while the backend sees a list that fails its allow-list and is reflected into the error path" — the victim's own request returns the stored payload.
opening_mechanisms.htb-proxy-smuggling-exec-stderr-oracle: Two openings, both about a hand-written gate that inspects something other than what it forwards: "blacklistCheck tests for the substrings localhost, 0.0.0.0, 127. ... a string test over the raw bytes, not a parse of the destination address" (beaten by 0af405cf.nip.io), and "bodySplit := strings.Split(raw, \"\\r\\n\\r\\n\") and then validates only bodySplit[1]" while the proxy writes the whole original buffer upstream.
opening_mechanisms.htb-quickblog-codefence-xss-registration: The client-side renderer's escaping decides the sink: "read the client-side renderer, not the server template, and write down exactly which characters it escapes. If '<' is escaped but '>' is not, the sink is an attribute rather than a tag" — so the payload must be a self-firing attribute (autofocus plus onfocus), fired by the privileged browser that visits the page.
opening_mechanisms.htb-resizer-filename-traversal-olefile-s: The supplied filename is the filesystem path: "upload once, upload the same name again, and upload a path-equivalent form such as ./name. A duplicate-file rejection on the equivalent form proves the raw filename is used and the check is path-based" — the write lands wherever the name points, and the rejection doubles as a file-existence oracle.
opening_mechanisms.htb-sos-or-sso-vue-vbind-onerror-xss-sup: A front-end framework hands attacker-chosen attributes to the DOM: "when a framework renders stored content through a dynamic component that binds an attribute object, test an on-handler attribute" — Vue refuses to set an /^on[a-z]/ key as a property when the value is a string, so it becomes a real inline handler in the reviewer bot's session.
opening_mechanisms.htb-spell-orsterra-nginx-unixsocket-redi: The server builds an outbound connection out of an untrusted string: "GET /assets/127.0.0.1:80/ and confirm the app's own page comes back" proves proxy_pass http://$1 is a full SSRF, and because nginx accepts unix:<path>:<uri> and percent-decodes the URI, the decoded bytes become literal protocol tokens for the internal line-protocol service.
opening_mechanisms.htb-ssos-oauth-registration-race-cookie-: Win the registration ordering on an identifier the application will later claim itself: "win a registration race on a fixed account (e.g. student@domain) by hammering POST /api/register with your own password before the bot's startup sequence reaches its own registerUser for the same account" — owning it makes the bot's own login fail and leaves the shared token on your account.
opening_mechanisms.htb-unearthly-shop-aggregation-pipeline-: The decoded request body is handed to the driver as the whole query structure: "check whether the database helper calls an aggregation rather than a find, and whether the request body reaches it whole" — "a controlled pipeline is strictly more than a controlled filter: it reads other collections and, through its write stages, modifies them".
opening_mechanisms.htb-weather-app-ssrf-crlf-request-smuggl: A request field is interpolated into a fetched URL without encoding: "place unicode characters that the URL parser folds into space, carriage return and line feed inside the interpolated field", then "append a full registration request to the loopback origin with an exact content length" — the backend issues the request, so the loopback-only restriction is satisfied.
opening_mechanisms.htb-why-lambda-complaint-vhtml-xss-bot-k: The rendering directive, not the template text, is the sink: "find where the privileged browser renders attacker input, and check the rendering directive rather than the template text" — an interpolation passed to an HTML-rendering directive executes only an event handler, not a script tag, and the injected script then runs same-origin as the bot.

coverage_note: classify.py is expected to name a class for each opening_mechanism below. Two do not, and both are structural rather than missing signals: bonechewercon-method-not-allowed opens on reading an unhandled error page, which belongs to web-info-disclosure — a registry skill that is not a bug class, so classify.py can never return it; and imagetok opens on "the signature does not cover all of the signed data" (bcrypt truncating at 72 bytes), a mechanism the taxonomy has no class for at all. Coverage measured 2026-09-26: 22 of 24.
